Debugging helpers

Source: R/debug_utils.R
print_family.Rd

print_family() prints a mobject and, indented by one tab per level, every submobject below it, each with its name and id.

Usage

print_family(mobject, n_tabs = 0)

index_labels(
  mobject,
  label_height = 0.15,
  background_stroke_width = 5,
  background_stroke_color = BLACK,
  ...
)

Arguments

mobject

A mobject.

n_tabs

Indentation of the first line, in tabs.

label_height

Height of each label.

background_stroke_width, background_stroke_color

Outline drawn behind each label.

...

Further arguments passed to Integer().

Value

print_family() returns mobject invisibly; index_labels() returns a VGroup of labels.

Details

index_labels() returns a VGroup() of Integer() labels, one placed on each submobject of mobject, which helps when picking parts of a complicated mobject such as a MathTex(). The labels count from 1, as mobject[i] does in R (upstream labels count from 0). Labels go on the submobjects, the parts mobject[i] returns; upstream labels the pieces of split(), which also include mobject itself when it has points of its own. Each label is scaled to label_height and gets a background stroke so it stays legible on top of the mobject.

Examples

print_family(VGroup(Square(), VGroup(Circle(), Dot())))
#>  VGroup 23ff2af6d2bfa8af98-1962
#> 	 Square 23ff2af6d2bfa8af98-1957
#> 	 VGroup 23ff2af6d2bfa8af98-1961
#> 		 Circle 23ff2af6d2bfa8af98-1959
#> 		 Dot 23ff2af6d2bfa8af98-1960
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Needs LaTeX and dvisvgm.
eq <- MathTex("\\frac{d}{dx}f(x)g(x)=")
labels <- index_labels(eq[1])
} # }
